desc: Derive formulas: compute prefix distinct array L[1..N] and suffix distinct array R[2..N] (R[k] = distinct count of A[k..N]) using sets/last-occurrence.

Design the segment tree: base value for candidate split i is L[i]; when processing right endpoint j (element x=A[j]), range-add +1 to all i in [prev[x], j-1] where prev[x] is previous occurrence index of x (0 if none), since middle segment (i+1..j) gains x as new distinct exactly for those i.
Implement brute force O(N²) reference solution for validation on small arrays.

Implement main solution: precompute L[] and R[], sweep j with lazy segment tree over i; activate position i=j-1 before each query; range-add +1 on [prev[A[j]], j-1]; candidate = querymax(0, j-1) + R[j+1].
Fix syntax errors in `pull` (`mx[p < 1 | 1]`, `mx[p << 1 |< 1]` → `mx[p << 1 | 1]`) so the submitted code actually compiles and runs.
Re-run cross-validation of the corrected code: exhaustive n=3..8 over {1,2,3}, random arrays, both samples, and edge cases (N=3, all identical → 3, all distinct → N).

Confirm final solution uses fast I/O, adequate recursion limit (or increase sys.setrecursionlimit for the recursive segtree with N=3×10^5), O(N log N) time / O(N) memory, reads stdin and writes answer to stdout.
